content:
maria: Quick sync — I'm rethinking the breadcrumb contract for the new console nav. We need a small set of rules for deep links into collapsed sidebar groups and predictable back-button behavior.

jon: Agree. The current approach (hash fragments for anchors) breaks history and keyboard focus when sections are collapsed.

ash: Can you sketch the main problems?

maria: 1) Deep links like `/projects/42/models#model-embed` often land on a collapsed group so the anchor scrolls nowhere. 2) Using `#` means clicking a link doesn't create a full router entry, so back/forward feels inconsistent. 3) Focus isn't moved to the revealed item — a11y fail.

sam: TLDR: we need deterministic expansion + focus on deep-link open. :+1:

emily: My vote is path-based deep links instead of hashes: `/projects/42/models/model-embed` or `/projects/42/models?anchor=model-embed`. Cleaner for analytics and routing.

jon: Path-based is nicer but we should avoid exploding routes for every nested item. Leaning to using query param `?anchor=` that our router treats as a nav action (pushState) instead of a pure fragment.

maria: Proposal: adopt these rules — (A) deep links can use `?anchor=` or explicit path segments; (B) router treats anchor as actionable: expand relevant sidebar group, scroll to element, move focus to the target node and set `aria-current` on the crumb; (C) anchors create a history entry so back button collapses back.

ash: Implementation details: router middleware should parse `anchor`, compute target node id, call expandGroup(id), then `requestAnimationFrame` -> `element.focus()` with `tabindex=-1` fallback. Also set `role="link"` or `aria-current="true"` on the crumb.

emily: Question: what about sharing links with query params removed (analytics)? We should canonicalize to path where logical (e.g., `/models/:modelId`). For ephemeral UI anchors (like long list positions) keep `?anchor=`.

sam: Also need to handle deep links into modals and flyouts — if target is inside a modal, open the modal first. Edge case: modal state must be encoded in the URL (e.g., `/projects/42/models?modal=info&anchor=model-embed`).

jon: Accessibility nits: ensure focus trap isn't invoked before we focus the anchored element. Use `inert` on other panels while focusing. And announce via live region: "Navigated to Model embed — section expanded" for screen readers.

access-bot: Accessibility checklist reminder:
- Move focus to target when navigation occurs
- Ensure `aria-current` on current crumb
- Provide live region announcement for reveal actions
- Keyboard reachable toggle for collapsed groups (Enter/Space)

maria: UX question — breadcrumbs semantics. Should crumb items reflect visible grouping (i.e., show collapsed group name) or reflect logical path (full path even if intermediate is collapsed)?

emily: I think breadcrumbs should show logical path but collapse intermediate slashes into an overflow pill when narrow. Example: `Projects / Acme Corp / Models / Model Embed` — even if `Acme Corp` group is collapsed in the sidebar, the crumb still shows it.

jon: Agree. Breadcrumbs = logical path; sidebar = interaction surface. They can diverge visually but must map 1:1 for deep linking.

ash: For URL routing, we should document router invariants in the PR:
```
// invariants
1. URL reflects logical resource: /projects/:pid/models/:mid
2. UI state (expansion/selected) is derived from URL when possible
3. transient UI only uses hash when it's truly ephemeral (focus jump)
```

sam: One more: when expanding groups via deep link, we should animate (slide open) but do not steal the scroll — avoid sudden jumps. Use `scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'center'})`.

maria: Nice. Can we land on a small decision doc for the console nav RFC? I can draft a one-pager with examples and code suggestions: path vs query vs fragment examples, a11y checklist, and a set of unit/integration tests to add.

emily: Please include these test cases: deep-link expands group, back button collapses, focus moves and is announced, shared link opens correctly for teammates without JS disabled.

jon: Dev note — add e2e tests in Playwright that run with reduced throttling, assert `history.length` changes, and that `aria-current` is present after nav.

maria: I'll draft a doc and link a prototype build. Expect a preview link later today.

ux-bot: Preview deploy queued — https://console-preview.redwood.ai/1979991234-nav-anchors (expires in 48h)

sam: Quick microcopy nit: breadcrumb items should use sentence-case not ALL-CAPS. Small win.

emily: +1 on sentence case. Also ensure tooltip text for truncated breadcrumb includes full path for screen reader users.

maria: Cool. Action items: I will: 1) publish RFC draft, 2) add a11y checklist, 3) attach example routes and router middleware pseudocode. Jon/ash/sam/emily — please review and toss in any missing edge cases.

jon: I'll look at router middleware and tests.

ash: I'll prototype the focus/animation sequence.

sam: I'll add copy + a11y tooltip text.

emily: I'll verify breadcrumb visuals and responsive truncation.

maria: Thanks — closing thread for now, will ping when doc is live. :pray:
